configured folder adr 0118 — browser-driven runner setup: an ed25519 device key as a second runner-ticket credential, a github releases proxy for the binary, and the file system access api for a one-click configured folder status: accepted date: 2026-08-27 context: closes the friction of setting up brabo-runner on the user's machine — until now it required manually assembling three things scattered across different screens: the project id, the folder path, and a personal access token minted on a third screen references (without editing): adr 0103 (the runner itself and its security boundary), adr 0104 (executionmode: runner, the pat backlog item this adr's device key complements), adr 0105 (the pat this decision is additive to, never a replacement), adr 0106 and adr 0112 (the standalone binaries this adr's proxy serves), adr 0107 (folder browsing through an already-connected runner — this adr is about getting the runner connected in the first place) context executionmode: runner (adr 0104) lets a project's code live in a folder on the user's own machine, with no bind-mount and no container — but reaching that state meant a person had to, by hand: find the project's id, generate a personal access token on project settings → access tokens (adr 0105), copy a brabo-runner --project <id --dir <path --token <token command someone had typed correctly, download the right binary for their os/architecture themselves, and run it from the right folder. three pieces of information, three screens, and a secret the user had to type or paste into a terminal. newprojectwizard.tsx and runneronboardingpanel.tsx had independently grown their own command text for this over time, and they had drifted apart — the wizard's copy never included --token at all, and the panel's copy used pnpm --filter runner start syntax instead of the binary. neither was wrong when written; nothing forced the two surfaces to agree, so they silently stopped agreeing. the product owner also asked, explicitly, whether the runner could discover a local docker/kubernetes container on its own and connect over ssh instead of needing a human to walk through any setup at all. that path was considered and rejected in this same session — see "alternatives considered and rejected" below. decision 1. an ed25519 device key, generated in the browser, is a second credential for runner-ticket — additive to the pat, never a replacement new table runnerdevicekeys (apps/api/src/db/schema.ts:2058-2081, migration 0054demonicshiverman.sql): id, userid (fk users, cascade), projectid (fk projects, cascade), name, publickeyjwk, createdat, revokedat, revokedreason, lastusedat — the public half of an ed25519 key pair the browser generates with crypto.subtle.generatekey (apps/web/src/lib/runner-bootstrap.ts:123-131). the private half never leaves the browser over the network; only the exported public jwk is posted to registerrunnerdevicekeyusecase (apps/api/src/application/use-cases/auth/register-runner-device-key.use-case.ts) via post /projects/:projectid/runner-device-keys (apps/api/src/interfaces/http/runner/runner-device-keys.controller.ts). that route is authenticated by the normal session jwt, @requirerole('developer') — the caller here really is the logged-in browser registering the device it's about to configure, the mirror image of personalaccesstokenscontroller issuing a pat. revokerunnerdevicekeyusecase deletes (marks revoked) the same way revokepersonalaccesstokenusecase does — idempotent, null for "not found or not yours," same non-disclosure discipline as rn-426. patauthguard — the same guard post .../runner-ticket already used for the pat (adr 0105, rn-439) — grew a second branch (apps/api/src/interfaces/http/auth/pat-auth.guard.ts:104-116): a bearer token starting with brb takes the existing pat p

t: ADR 0119 — Images published to GHCR on every final tag, and the production overlay pinned by digest
x: adr 0119 — images published to ghcr on every final tag, and the production overlay pinned by digest adr 0119 — images published to ghcr on every final tag, and the production overlay pinned by digest status: accepted date: 2026-08-29 references (without editing): adr 0025 and adr 0027 (both recorded "publishing the image to a registry" as out of scope — this adr is what closes it), adr 0030 (the push exceptions this decision deliberately does not extend), adr 0036 (the version baked into the artifact, which is why version stays separate from tag). context release.yml built the four production images on every final tag with load: true and push: false, and said so in a comment: the build existed to prove the tag was buildable, and publishing would "come in when the registry is decided". meanwhile the production overlay pointed at ghcr.io/owner/brabo- with newtag: replacewithdigest — an owner placeholder and a marker no step ever substituted. the consequence was not cosmetic. as long as it held, "production deploy executable end to end" was false, and everything behind it stayed behind it: a real rollout, a restore rehearsed against production images, and the runner binary's code-signing story (which needs a published artifact to sign). an external review of the repository ranked it the most expensive declared debt, and this adr is that item. a second defect surfaced while doing it: the overlay's images: block listed three images, not four. brabo-backup was never remapped, so the backup cronjob inherited brabo-backup:prod from the base — a name that resolves in no registry. the environment that most needs its backup would have been the one whose backup pod never started. the ci never caught it because the overlay check validates that the overlay builds, and a locally-named image builds fine. decision 1. release.yml publishes the four images to ghcr on every final tag. login uses the job's own githubtoken with packages: write — no new secret to rotate, and the scope dies with the job. packages are public: the code is already public in the same repository, secrets are never baked into an image (the four sibling keys refuse to boot with an example value, rn-114), and public packages keep the production overlay pull-and-go, with no imagepullsecret to create, reference and rotate in every namespace. 2. the registry prefix is a bake variable, not a second bakefile. registry defaults to "", so ci.yml keeps building the short local names (brabo-api:prod) it scans and smoke-tests; release.yml sets ghcr.io/<owner/. the trailing slash lives in the value — an empty prefix has to produce exactly the old name, and any fixed separator in the interpolation would have broken ci.yml. output follows the same shape: type=docker (load locally) by default, type=registry (push) for the release. type=registry is not an optimization — it is the only mode in which bake returns containerimage.digest, because the digest is born from the push. 3. what each tag published is recorded by digest in .release/images.json. tags (3.2.0, the commit sha) are still published: they are for human conversation and manual docker pull. they are never what a manifest references — a mutable tag pointing at different content over time destroys deterministic rollback and lets two pods of the same replicaset run different binaries, which is what the overlay's own comment had said since phase 5. 4. the file is an asset of the github release, and rides the changelog pr into the repository. it does not get a third push exception. the branch policy has exactly two (tags by the release bot, .release/gate.json by the gate bot), and a mechanism that needs a new exception every time it grows is a mechanism that stops being a policy. the release asset is the authoritative copy, available the instant the tag exists; the versioned copy arrives through the pr release.yml already opens against dev. 5. the overlay keeps the marker; make imagens-do-release applies the digest. the repository do

t: ADR 0120 — Browser E2E against the production compose, in a package outside the workspace
x: adr 0120 — browser e2e against the production compose, in a package outside the workspace adr 0120 — browser e2e against the production compose, in a package outside the workspace status: accepted date: 2026-08-29 references (without editing): adr 0032 (the cookie session this layer exists to prove), adr 0117 (the precedent for a dev-only subtree with its own lockfile), adr 0027 (the production smoke this reuses instead of duplicating). context the test pyramid was strong at the bottom and had a hole at the top. the api has 142 specs, the engine 126, the web tests component by component under jsdom, and docker/smoke.sh proves over http that the four production images boot and talk to each other. none of those exercises a browser. and the mechanisms that carry the session are browser mechanisms: the access token lives in memory and the refresh in an httponly cookie, paired with a readable brabocsrf sent as x-csrf-token; the web is served from :8088 and the api answers on :3000, so every authenticated call is cross-origin — preflight, samesite, credentials: 'include'; the session channel needs a single-use ticket (rn-108) and a real websocket handshake against the engine, on a third origin. jsdom has none of that. it has no real origin, does no preflight, and httponly is not a thing it can enforce — a test asserting the refresh is unreadable would pass there while proving nothing. apps/api/src/main.ts already carries the comment that says it plainly: "teste nao faz preflight." this is not a hypothetical gap. it's where the last cookie, cors and socket bugs actually appeared, and each was found by hand. decision a browser e2e layer, in e2e/, running against the production compose that ci already brings up. three parts to the decision, each with its own reason. it runs against docker-compose.prod.yml, not vite dev the cross-origin split (:8088 → :3000 → :4000) exists only in the production compose. running against the dev server would exercise a topology nobody deploys and would silently stop proving the one thing this layer is for. so the job reuses docker/smoke.sh with smokekeepup=1: same images, same compose, one build. it also runs in the same ci job as the images. the four images are most of that job's wall clock; a separate job would rebuild them to exercise the identical stack. e2e/ is not a member of the pnpm workspace same shape as website/ (adr 0117): its own pnpm-workspace.yaml and pnpm-lock.yaml, installed with pnpm install from inside the folder, driven from the root by pnpm --dir e2e. the reason is the same one: playwright's tree never reaches any product image, and leaving it in the root lockfile would make the product's pnpm audit report test tooling as if it were shipped surface. the difference from the website — that this package tests the product — doesn't change the argument, because what decides is where the dependency goes, not what it talks about. it proves mechanisms, not screens the specs assert on observable mechanism: the httponly flag as the browser reports it, document.cookie as the page sees it, survival across a reload, the websocket url carrying ticket=. selectors are structural (input[type="email"]), never text — the interface language is decided by the server, and a test pinned to "sign in" would break on a language change, a failure that says nothing about the product. seeding (workspace → project → session) goes over http, mirroring smoke.sh. the browser is expensive and the project wizard is not what this layer exists to prove; slow setup is setup that gets switched off. consequences the gap closes for the paths that only a browser reaches. both specs were proven by mutation: a wrong password turns the auth specs red, and pointing the socket assertion at a path that doesn't exist fails with "nenhum websocket foi aberto contra o engine." the images job grows: pnpm/node setup, a chromium download, and the run itself. in exchange it stays one job and one image build. chromium only. one browser pro

t: ADR 0121 — The schema split by domain aggregate, behind a barrel
x: adr 0121 — the schema split by domain aggregate, behind a barrel adr 0121 — the schema split by domain aggregate, behind a barrel status: accepted date: 2026-08-29 references (without editing): adr 0038 and adr 0053 (the aggregate boundaries this split mirrors), adr 0117 (same shape of reasoning: a boundary is worth drawing when the shared thing charges a price nobody chose to pay). context apps/api/src/db/schema.ts was 2 452 lines holding 51 pgtable declarations and 34 pgenum declarations — everything from users to huggingfacemodelpullrequests, from the event log to the rag chunks. this was already declared technical debt. docs/architecture.md's debt table has carried a row for it since the table existed: "the repo's most-changed file … concentrates the tables into a single file", with the consequence spelled out in the row itself — a second collaborator touching the schema at the same time hits a conflict, guaranteed, because every schema change lands in the same file regardless of which part of the product it belongs to. the number in that row (35 tables) was already stale by 16 tables, which is its own evidence: the file grew faster than the paragraph describing it. three concrete costs, none of them hypothetical: every merge of two schema changes is a textual conflict, even when the two changes are in unrelated aggregates — an auth column and a backlog constraint have nothing to do with each other and still meet in the same hunk. git log --follow on the schema is useless. the file's history is the union of every product area's history, so "when did chunks change and why" requires reading commits about refreshtokens. reading it requires knowing where to scroll. the file was already internally organised by // --- section --- comments that named product areas — the split doesn't invent a taxonomy, it promotes one the file was already keeping by hand. decision 1. one file per domain aggregate, under apps/api/src/db/schema/ the buckets mirror apps/api/src/domain/, the aggregate boundaries the codebase already commits to. no new taxonomy: if the domain layer has a folder for it, the schema has a file with that name. file tables enums iam.ts 5 4 sessions.ts 5 5 llm.ts 7 6 actions.ts 1 2 agents.ts 4 1 instructions.ts 2 0 backlog.ts 3 3 architecture.ts 2 0 git.ts 3 5 psychologist.ts 2 0 anamnese.ts 4 0 auth.ts 9 3 rag.ts 1 1 containers.ts 1 1 huggingface.ts 1 1 backup.ts 1 2 total 51 34 three placements needed a decision rather than a lookup, and each one is recorded as a comment at the top of the file that owns it: handoffs goes to sessions.ts, not agents.ts. the entity is domain/sessions/handoff.entity.ts: a handoff only exists inside a session, and the domain layer already said so. usercredentials goes to llm.ts, not iam.ts or git.ts, even though credentialprovider spans llm keys and git tokens. the entity is domain/llm/user-credential.entity.ts and domain/git has no counterpart — the split follows the domain layer, including where the domain layer's own choice is a compromise. backup.ts is the one file with no matching domain/ folder. backup is operational infrastructure with no business rule of its own. forcing it into architecture.ts or containers.ts would have made the mapping lie about what an aggregate is, to avoid a 60-line file. a small honest file costs less than a wrong boundary. 2. enums live with the table that calls them, because the module graph has to stay acyclic a cross-file foreign key is safe under a cycle: .references(() = othertable.column) takes a lazy callback precisely so forward references resolve. a cross-file enum is not: storypromotionmodeenum('storypromotion') runs at module-evaluation time, and a cycle whose edge points the wrong way throws referenceerror: cannot access '…' before initialization at import, not at query time. so three enums sit where their only caller sits, rather than where a subject grouping would put them: projectexecutionmode and storypromotion live in iam.ts, not git.ts/backlog

t: ADR 0122 — `SessionPage.tsx` split into five mechanical PRs, declared upfront
x: adr 0122 — `sessionpage.tsx` split into five mechanical prs, declared upfront adr 0122 — sessionpage.tsx split into five mechanical prs, declared upfront status: accepted date: 2026-08-29 references (without editing): adr 0121 (same shape of reasoning as this one — a shared file grew past the point where "just work around it" is cheaper than drawing a boundary — but a different execution shape: 0121 was one zero-diff commit, this is five prs in sequence, because the file is under active feature churn and a single pr would either freeze the codebase or race every other change). context apps/web/src/routes/sessionpage.tsx is 3 807 lines and 169 kib — docs/explanation/backlog.md's technical-debt review already carries a row for it: decompose sessionpage.tsx / projectsettingstab.tsx g sessionpage.tsx is 169 kib with 25 test files importing it; projectsettingstab.tsx is 90 kib already informally called a "disputed file" in historico-de-fases.md, but never promoted to a tracked debt item; per the standing rule this is its own phase, never a drive-by refactor three concrete costs make this more than a size complaint: 25 test files depend on it (sessionpage..test.tsx plus sessionpage.ponto.test.ts) — any structural change risks a wide blast radius, and the size of the file makes it hard to tell in advance which of the 25 a given change can touch. the file is under active churn, not legacy code. 50 commits have touched it; the most recent 15 are almost entirely feat additions (structured questions, handoff, the turn-activity strip, the rn-172 turn/desfecho ordering…), and none of them was an extraction — this is the first attempt at drawing an internal boundary in the file's history. that rules out a big-bang rewrite: freezing the file for one large pr would either block every other feature landing in it or force painful, repeated rebases. the test suite already draws part of the boundary. before this pr, sessionpage.ordenacao-e-avisos.test.tsx imports aberturasdeturno, turnodoseq, afundardesfechos, ordemdaacaonatimeline and agruparnarracoesdoturno directly by name from ./sessionpage (await import('./sessionpage'), destructured), and sessionpage.ponto.test.ts does the same for pontodasessao — not through rendering the component, but as plain function calls. the tests had already decided these five (plus agruparnarracoesdoturno) are independent units; this adr promotes that existing boundary to a real module boundary instead of inventing a new one. given the churn and the blast radius, the standing rule from claude.md applies — "not a drive-by refactor" — so this is its own phase, planned as a sequence of independently-mergeable, behavior-neutral prs, each one evidenced by the same 25 test files passing unedited. decision five prs, executed and merged one at a time (never in parallel — each one lands on dev before the next starts), in this order: pure timeline/turn helpers → apps/web/src/lib/session-timeline.ts (this pr). aberturasdeturno, turnodoseq, afundardesfechos, pontodasessao, ordemdaacaonatimeline, and the timelineentry type they share. all five are confirmed pure — no jsx, no styles/css-module reference, no closure over component state — which makes this the lowest-risk slice and the right one to go first: a mechanical .ts move with nothing to reconcile against react's render cycle. agruparnarracoesdoturno stays in sessionpage.tsx on purpose, even though it sits in the same region and is tested the same way: it returns jsx (<disclosure) and reads three styles.narracoes class names from sessionpage.module.css. moving it would mean deciding that lib/ accepts its first .tsx file — today it holds only .ts sources (a few .tsx tests exist, but zero .tsx source files) — and that precedent belongs to a pr that is actually about jsx sub-components (pr 2), not one that is supposed to be a pure-function move. storyslide → apps/web/src/routes/storyslide.tsx. the first jsx sub-component to move, and the simplest one: a single leaf component

t: ADR 0123 — Golden-set of regression cases for the QA Automation agent's semantic judgment
x: adr 0123 — golden-set of regression cases for the qa automation agent's semantic judgment adr 0123 — golden-set of regression cases for the qa automation agent's semantic judgment status: accepted date: 2026-08-30 references (without editing): adr 0020 (the finding this closes — its own acceptance criterion documents the qa gate's semantic step as non-deterministic with a local model, and names the fix direction this adr builds: "point at an api model instead of hoping"). context adr 0020 closed the pr gates' acceptance criterion, but with a caveat spelled out in its own title section: closed, but not deterministic. against local qwen2.5-coder:7b, the criterion — qa matching a business rule to a test, twice on the same pr — closed only on the 10th of 11 runs. the 11th, run immediately after with no code change, did not close: the model ended the loop without calling emitqaverdict. adr 0020 names this explicitly as the semantic step being "the role that fits worst in a small model" and states the fix direction without building it: "point demoqamodel at an api model." that direction never became a mechanism — it stayed documented, not built. an external code review of this session's work, ranked 15 findings by priority; 14 of 15 closed as this session progressed. the 15th and last was this one, proposed with no build cost attached: "a golden-set (5-10 cases, loose expected output, fixed model, allow-failure to start) would turn 'the demo depends on a 7b's judgment' into a trend signal." three facts, confirmed by reading code rather than assumed, shaped what could be built today: the judgment can be invoked in isolation, without the full state machine. engine.gates.qaautomacaoagent.run/5 is already called this way in qaautomacaoagenttest.exs — no qaleadserver, no gatestate, no pr, no git repository, no backlog. the only thing separating that existing test from a real golden-set is swapping the fake llm client for the real one. the real client requires the api actually running, reachable. engine.sessions.engineapiclient.live.llmturn/5 reads application.fetchenv!(:engine, :apiurl), populated only by config/runtime.exs (via apiurl) — never by config/test.exs. this is not a unit test in the usual sense: it is, in practice, "run against the dev stack," the same posture demo-pr-gates.ts already has. ci is not possible today — confirmed, not assumed. zero mention of ollama in .github/workflows/; the compose service sits behind profiles: ["local-llm"], never started by docker/smoke.sh. zero llm secret in the repository. and the ci's own culture rejects silent allow-failure: pr-police.yml is the only place in the repo using continue-on-error, and even there the error is re-raised in a final step. there is no check today that can go red with no consequence. wiring this into ci needs an api llm secret or new infrastructure (a gpu runner, an ollama pull step) — a decision for a human, not something to build by choosing. decision where it lives. apps/engine/test/engine/gates/qaautomacaoagentgoldentest.exs, use engine.datacase, reusing the same devstate/devcontext construction as qaautomacaoagenttest.exs. it is exunit, not a new mix task: there is no mix.task of its own anywhere in apps/engine/lib today, and an isolated test is already this codebase's natural shape for this class of thing — unlike the api side, where demo-pr-gates.ts is a script because no "call the function directly" equivalent exists there. a permanent exclusion tag, never availability detection. the testhelper.exs pattern for gitleaks/hadolint/yamllint/actionlint auto-includes a tagged test when the binary is found on the machine — right for a free, deterministic tool, and wrong here. this development machine already has ollama running continuously; auto-inclusion by reachability would make the golden-set fire inside any mix test, spending tokens with no warning and introducing real flakiness in a suite that is 100% deterministic today. only mix test --only goldensetqa runs

t: ADR 0127 — Two downgrade ceilings on `project_members`, and the override stays
x: adr 0127 — two downgrade ceilings on `project_members`, and the override stays adr 0127 — two downgrade ceilings on projectmembers, and the override stays context resolveeffectiveroleusecase.forproject has been, since phase 1, projectrole ?? workspacerole: when there is a row in projectmembers, it wins, without comparing it with the workspace role. the override applies in both directions — up and down. this was discovered by the review of 444, which closed the role gate of the members section, and is recorded in rn-471. the finding has two halves. the first is documentary: four places promised the opposite — "the effective role is the higher of this one and what the person already has in the workspace", "associating someone as viewer here doesn't downgrade a workspace owner" — three openapi descriptions and a comment in apps/web/src/lib/roles.ts. rn-471 fixed the web one (it was the worst: it lived in the module that exports roleatleast and roleorder, that is, in the code the next person in this family opens before anything else) and declared the three in the api as not fixed, because they are a contract change. the second half was not kept anywhere, and it is the reason for this adr: with the override applying downward, addprojectmemberusecase was a one-line passthrough to the repository upsert and removeprojectmemberusecase only checked whether the project existed. neither of them looked at who the target is nor at the relation between actor and target. two consequences reachable by any maintainer, today: downgrading the workspace owner. a maintainer writes viewer for the owner in a project and the owner loses their own project — the dashboard read, the decisions, everything. restoring it requires maintainer, which the owner just lost in that scope; irreversible self-downgrade. a maintainer writes themselves as viewer and cannot undo it, because undoing is the same route, which requires maintainer. there is no way back through the screen. none of this is privilege escalation — nobody gains a role they did not have. it is loss of access, and the difference matters: a maintainer could already do damage in the project, but could not produce a state from which nobody leaves without going to the database. the obvious path would be to make forproject return "the higher of the two" and erase the problem at the root, aligning the code with the three descriptions instead of the other way around. it was considered and rejected: restricting someone in a sensitive project — a workspace developer who becomes viewer in project x — is a deliberate product capability, and it is the only way that exists to contain access per project. "the higher of the two" eliminates it, and resolve-effective-role.use-case.spec.ts has always pinned the upward half ("project role overrides the workspace one"). decision the override stays in both directions, and the two dangerous moves are now refused. forproject does not change: it remains projectrole ?? workspacerole, and remains the only composition of that role in the system. ceiling 1 — nobody downgrades whoever is workspace owner. the role requested for someone whose workspace role is owner must be owner; anything below is 403. writing project owner for someone who is already workspace owner is redundant and passes — only the downgrade is refused. the owner is read from workspacemembers.role, never from workspaces.createdby. both exist in db/schema/iam.ts and are not the same thing. createdby is a historical fact: who created the workspace. it is the role that authorization uses everywhere else in the system — resolveeffectiveroleusecase.forworkspace is workspaces.findmemberrole, and createdby appears in no authorization path (it appears in get-credential-spend.use-case.ts, to know whose llm key is being spent, which is another question). a ceiling that read createdby would protect the wrong person in two concrete and opposite cases: the creator who already transferred ownership and is now developer wou

t: ADR 0128 — The Docker port, and the packaging proof that chose the implementation
x: adr 0128 — the docker port, and the packaging proof that chose the implementation adr 0128 — the docker port, and the packaging proof that chose the implementation context the real-container execution plan has two places that need to talk to a docker daemon: the runner (the docker of the user's machine, for a project in runner mode) and a server broker yet to be born (pr 1.2, for a project in container mode). the api never receives the socket, and that is a closed decision. the choice of library was conditioned on a proof, not on a preference. dockerode is the de facto node client for docker, but the runner is distributed through three paths — cloning the monorepo, npm install -g @brabo/runner (adr 0106) and a standalone binary via bun build --compile (adr 0112) — and the third is the most fragile of the three: it already needed its own manifest generator (scripts/build-bin.mjs) to embed the .node of node-pty, because bun only embeds a file reached by a static specifier. the tree that dockerode@5 drags in is large — docker-modem, ssh2, @grpc/grpc-js, protobufjs, tar-fs — and ssh2 carries an optional native binding (cpu-features). hence the order the product owner set: prove first, design later, with the decision already written for both outcomes — green, dockerode stays; broken, the runner falls back to execfile('docker', …) and this adr records the exact error as the reason. no bundler patch or shim: a creative workaround here becomes debt nobody understands later. decision the proof, and what it returned dockerode@5.0.1 + @types/dockerode@4.0.1 went into apps/runner, with an adapter that imports, instantiates (new docker()) and calls (ping()) — exercised by a --self-test-docker flag run against the artifacts, never by an import the bundler could erase. step result pnpm --filter runner build (tsup) passed — but tsup leaves dependencies as external require (that is how jose already lives today), so dockerode did not even enter the bundle pnpm --filter runner smoke passed — node dist/index.cjs --self-test-docker resolved dockerode from nodemodules and talked to the daemon pnpm --filter runner build:bin (bun build --compile) failed the error, pasted whole: the chain is mandatory, not accidental — it was read in the installed code, not assumed: lib/modem.js does require('./ssh') at the top of the module: the ssh transport enters the graph even in this runner, which only talks to the local unix socket. the require of cpu-features is wrapped in try/catch inside ssh2 and degrades gracefully at runtime — but whoever resolves the graph here is the bundler, at build time, and a bundler has no try/catch. it is the same class of problem adr 0112 documented with node-pty, with one deciding difference: there the binding is essential (without it there is no terminal, and so it was worth building the embedding mechanism), and here it is optional acceleration of a transport we do not use. measured and not adopted, for the record: bun build --compile --external cpu-features compiles (280 modules against 79), produces a binary of 84 473 032 b (+1.7 mb) and dockerode works inside it — the ping answers against the real daemon, because the try/catch of ssh2 swallows the stub bun leaves in place. this is written so that nobody needs to redo the investigation, and it is exactly the workaround the product owner's decision excluded in advance: it drags an optional .node from a dead ssh tree into five binaries per platform, and the debt would be illegible six months later. therefore: the runner uses execfile('docker', …). dockerode was removed from package.json and from the lockfile; nothing of it remained in the tree. the broker (pr 1.2) does not inherit this decision — it runs in an image we build and never becomes a standalone binary, so dockerode remains a candidate there, and that is precisely why the port below exists. sizes, measured artifact before after delta dist/index.cjs 91 843 b 106 221 b +14 378 b (+15.7 %) dist-bin/brabo-runner-linux-x64

t: ADR 0129 — RAG search telemetry is a TABLE, with the weights frozen in the row
x: adr 0129 — rag search telemetry is a table, with the weights frozen in the row adr 0129 — rag search telemetry is a table, with the weights frozen in the row context apps/api/src/domain/rag/rag-search-limits.ts declares, in its own comment, that the four numbers of the hybrid search — the two weights (0.6/0.4), the threshold (0.2) and the number of candidates per signal — come from no calibration at all: nenhum dos quatro numeros abaixo vem de calibracao com dado real: nao ha, ainda, um corpo de perguntas reais rodado contra este indice. adr 0080 chose those values with the reasoning recorded (the scales of tsrank and cosine are not comparable, and the larger weight on the vector side compensates for the shorter ruler of the lexical one) and said they would be revisited with data. the data never came, and the reason was not lack of use: the search left no trace at all. zero table rows, zero rag. events in the whole product. without a trace, "calibrating" would be swapping one guess for another — and worse, it would be irreversible in practice, because there would be nothing to compare before and after. this is the first of the five stages of the measurable rag program, and it is deliberately the only one that does not change search behavior: it gives the eyes, and stops. the concrete obstacle the obvious way out would be a session event — the event log is already the measuring instrument for the rest of the product, and the claude.md rule says execution metrics are extracted from it by script, never by hand. but sessionevents.sessionid is not null (apps/api/src/db/schema/sessions.ts), and a search coming from the rag tab is a project one: it has no session at all. recording the telemetry only as an event would lose exactly the searches in which a human looked at the scores and judged — which are the ones that carry the only real signal the measurement can have. it is the same class of problem that forced the cut of embedding metering in adr 0075: tokenusage.sessionid is also not null, and indexing a repository does not happen inside a session. there the cut was declared and the spend was left out. here the cut would be worse: half the searches would remain, and the ones that remain are the agents' — the ones nobody judges. decision 1. two tables in apps/api/src/db/schema/rag.ts, not events. ragsearches (one row per search: hits with the 1-based rank of each chunk, degraded/vectoravailable, latencyms, actor, and a nullable sessionid) and ragfeedback (the util/irrelevante vote on a chunk of a search). the aggregate's file already existed (chunks), so there is no change in the db/schema.ts barrel; the ragverdict enum lives in the same file as the table that calls it, by the convention of adr 0121, and actorkind is reused from sessions.ts instead of redeclared. sessionid null is information, not absence of data: it means the search came from the tab. 2. the weights go frozen in the row. pesosvigentes() (domain/rag/rag-telemetry.ts) copies {vector, lexical, threshold} from the moment of the search into the record. it is the same discipline as the price frozen in metering (adr 0042) and the imageversion of projectcontainers (adr 0081). without the copy, the first calibration that touched ragsearchweightvector would make all previous measurement start meaning something else, silently — and "did it improve after the change?", the only question the telemetry exists to answer, would become impossible to ask with the data at hand. it is a function and not an exported constant on purpose: a shared constant would be the same object in every jsonb row in memory. 3. the event exists, and it is narration. rag.search and rag.feedback enter the event log only when there is a session — the agent's path —, so the timeline can narrate what it did. the asymmetry is declared instead of hidden: the table is the source of the measurement, the event is narration, and medir:rag never reads the event log. both types are written out in full at the emissio

t: ADR 0157 — The self-movement ceiling on the workspace upsert, and the self-promotion that was a loophole

was a loophole status accepted. it is the third in the line opened by adr 0127 and continued by adr 0156. it closes the last move the two left declared in writing, and revises one sentence of 0127: self-promotion, which it recorded in the consequences as a capability that stayed, is now refused. an accepted adr is not edited — this one references it and says what changed. it corresponds to brb-002, a security p1 of the maintainer's register. context the two previous adrs closed the three doors of projectmembers — the two write ones and the removal one — and each of them pointed, in so many words, to what was left open. 0127: downgrading the workspace owner in the workspace. ceiling 1 is about projectmembers. post workspaces/:workspaceid/members remains an upsert with no ceiling at all — same class of defect, scope above, not addressed here. and 0156, reaffirming: extending the ceiling to the workspace. post workspaces/:workspaceid/members is an upsert with no ceiling at all, as adr 0127 already declared (…) different scope, separate decision. the defect, measured. addworkspacememberusecase was a twelve-line pass-through: execute(workspaceid, userid, role) calling workspaces.addmember. it did not receive the actor, and the controller (@post(':workspaceid/members'), @requirerole('owner')) called it with the bare body, without @currentuser() — there was nothing with which to apply any ceiling, just as there was nothing on removal before 0156. it is the same class of defect one scope above, and it is more serious for two reasons that do not exist in the project: there is no level above to hold the fall. in the project, downgrading oneself drops the effective role to the workspace role, which often holds it. in the workspace the role is the role: an owner who writes themselves as viewer loses the whole workspace, and with it all projects, the llm spend that is theirs by rn-060, and the very ability to invite whoever would replace them; there is no member removal route to undo it by another path. workspacescontroller has no member @delete — 0156 had already measured that and used it as an argument not to extend the ceiling in that pr. undoing is this same route, which requires the freshly abandoned owner. there is no way back through the screen, nor through the api. the second half: self-promotion. adr 0127 wrote, in the list of what remained possible: self-promotion. a maintainer can write themselves as project owner. it was already possible before this adr and still is; the ceilings are about going down, and opening the question of going up here would have changed, in passing, a capability nobody asked to change. there was a test pinning this — "raising one's own role is not a downgrade and still passes" —, with a workspace maintainer writing themselves as project owner. the decision not to open the question in that pr was right by process, and the answer, now that it is open, is that it is a loophole. both halves are the same move — a person deciding alone what authority they have —, and the upper one is the only one of the two that escalates privilege: 0127 could say its ceilings were not about escalation ("nobody gains a role they did not have"), and about self-promotion that is false. a maintainer becomes project owner without anyone promoting them, and in a workspace with sensitive projects it is the difference between restricting and being unrestrictable. decision 1. the workspace upsert receives the actor and refuses self-movement. addworkspacememberusecase.execute becomes (workspaceid, atorid, alvoid, papel) — the same order addprojectmemberusecase has had since 0127 and removeprojectmemberusecase gained in 0156 —, the controller passes @currentuser(), and changing one's own role there is 403. 2. the ceiling does not count owners.

the v6.1.0 release assets do not bring docker/broker/dockerfile.prod nor the code of apps/broker/packages/docker-port, so a one-liner installation, which runs in a folder without a checkout (adr 0160), does not even have anything to build. a question whose "yes" has no image to bring up is worse than none: the person consents to the socket risk and receives a pull access denied. only --source=local (clean checkout, on a tag) could build the broker — and even there the installation compose does not have the service. the fix is the one adr 0150 already named as small and outside its scope: publish the broker as a fifth image (a target in the bake, an id in the manifest, one more signature), and only then the installer's question. it is left for its own front, and it is that front that reopens this half. install.sh was not touched by this adr. decision 1. the api says whether the installation has a broker, in the two routes the screen already reads brokerconfigurado: boolean enters two existing responses and no new route: get workspaces/:workspaceid/projects-base — the creation wizard's question

the arquiteto, and execution does not start without it status accepted. decided by the maintainer on 2026-09-18 (at-092). it revises the trigger of rn-522, which had been born to keep the promise of rn-541 ("the bootstrap is deferred until the arquiteto's handoff"). neither came from an adr — both were born from a direct request of the product owner and live only in docs/business-rules.md —, so this is the first structural record of the moment the repository is born. the provisioning mechanism does not change: it is the same provisionrepositoryusecase, idempotent by design since adr 0005, called by the same accepthandoffusecase. the handoff target rule of adr 0038 (an external handoff addresses only an area lead or an agent without an area) and the arquiteto → dev lead chain of adr 0053 remain intact. context a real v6.1.0 installation, on 2026-09-14, produced this sequence in the event log of a new project: 02:40:54 — the arquiteto (architect) proposes openadrpr three times. the repository does not exist yet, and the tool fails all three times. 02:43:53 — handoff.offered to infra and to dev-lead (the architecture readiness confirmation offers both, offerinfrahandoffusecase). only the infra one is accepted. the dev-lead one stays offered. 03:02:34 — post /projects/:id/execution/activate answers 201. projectrepositories, projectgitconnections and repobootstraps stay empty. the project stays without a repository forever. the two defects are independent, and rn-522 carried both: the trigger was after whoever needs the repository. the arquiteto is the first agent with a tool that writes to the repository (openadrpr), and the infra lead, activated by the arquiteto → infra handoff, is the second (openinfrapr). both work before the acceptance to the dev lead. rn-541 said "the repository is born when development starts", and development, measured by what the agents do, starts at the arquiteto. the only trigger was skippable. activating execution does not require an accepted handoff to the dev lead — it requires a current modulemap, and nothing else. whoever activates through the overview (or through the "activate execution" shortcut of the handoff card itself, rn-137) skips the acceptance, and with it the provisioning. nothing on the path refused. who hands off to the arquiteto, measured. the arquiteto can only be activated with an accepted handoff addressed to it (canactivateagent, domain/sessions/agent-activation.ts) — the exception is only the criativo (creative). the handoff is born through two doors, and both write through the same createhandoffusecase: the po, when finishing the backlog, with offerhandoff(toagent: "arquiteto") (the kickoff instruction in poserver.ex says so), or the user, through the manual handoff (requestmanualhandoffusecase, adr 0109). and the acceptance is a single one: accepthandoffusecase, the same one that already hosted rn-522's trigger. there is no path in which the arquiteto works without having gone through that acceptance. decision 1. the trigger becomes the acceptance of the handoff addressed to arquiteto. in accepthandoffusecase, the branch that calls provisionarrepositorio now fires for toagent === 'arquiteto', before activateagent — the same order rn-522 already used, for the same reason: the arquiteto wakes up in a project that already has somewhere to work, and the first openadrpr finds a repository. everything else in the branch stays byte for byte: always local (the only provider without credentials), a failure becomes repository.provisionfailed with an origin and never brings down the acceptance, an adopted repository leaves early without being a failure. 2. the old trigger stays, as a second idempotent door. the acceptance to dev-lead keeps calling the same provisioning. three reasons, in order of w

t: ADR 0166 — The routing preference lives in the model binding, travels with it, and freezes in metering
x: adr 0166 — the routing preference lives in the model binding, travels with it, and freezes in metering adr 0166 — the routing preference lives in the model binding, travels with it, and freezes in metering status accepted. decided by the maintainer on 2026-09-18 (at-090): "the routing preference is configurable per binding". it extends adr 0041 (capability in two layers, only declared when proven) and adr 0042 (what produced the number goes frozen in the tokenusage row). it edits neither. the rule born from here is rn-583. context measured in the tokenusage of the v6.1.0 installation (2026-09-14): 24 calls of ~deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-latest via openrouter. the upstreamprovider (rn-042) already said who served each one: relace in 23, with an average latency of 69.5 s (between 32 and 47 tok/s), and baidu in 1, with 37.8 s (~190 tok/s). openrouter chooses the upstream through a balancing that favors price when the request says nothing — and openrouter-provider.ts said nothing: the /chat/completions body went out without provider/sort. the hub accepts provider: { sort: "price" "throughput" "latency" } in the body. the remaining question is a product one, not a wire one: who chooses the criterion, and where that choice lives. decision 1. a column in the binding, in the llm aggregate routingpreference (enum routingpreference: price throughput latency), nullable, in modelbindings. null is today's behavior: nothing is sent and the hub decides on its own. the column enters apps/api/src/db/schema/llm.ts, where the binding already lives — the aggregate is the model's, and the enum lives with the two tables that call it (the enum rule of adr 0121). 2. the preference does not cascade on its own: it travels with the binding that won the cascade (session agent area project workspace, plus the criativo's (creative's) post-cascade step) remains a binding cascade. the winning binding brings the model and its preference; no level "inherits only the preference" from another. three reasons: the preference only makes sense together with the model with which it was chosen. it exists for one provider (the hub); cascading it separately would produce combinations nobody chose — the agent's model on a provider without the capability and the project's throughput, or the workspace's latency applied to a model the workspace owner never saw. an independent cascade would require a second chain on the screen. rn-470 made the model's chain visible node by node; two chains landing at different levels on the same row would be exactly the state the screen does not know how to explain. the level the cascade skips takes the preference with it. a binding skipped for unavailability or lack of tool calling stops being valid whole — model and criterion. having only the criterion survive would be the same defect as the first reason, created by the fall. written consequence: to put throughput on an entire area, one writes it on the area's binding; the agent that diverges with its own binding has its preference (null until someone chooses). 3. the write: absent preserves, null clears, a provider without the capability refuses put .../model-binding (all five scopes) gains routingpreference?: 'price' 'throughput' 'latency' null: absent — preserves the recorded preference, if the new model's provider accepts it; otherwise it becomes null. omitting cannot clear silently (that is how the usual model swap and "apply to all" keep calling the route), and it also cannot leave recorded a criterion the new provider does not understand; null — clears, explicitly; a value, with a provider without the capability — 422 (routingpreferencenotsupportederror), in the same filter as the other binding refusals. the request is well formed; what does not hold is the combination. the invariant the three rules sustain: no binding keeps a preference for a provider that does not declare it. 4. a provider capability, declared false while not proven llmprovidercapabilities.routingpreference, manda

t: ADR 0170 — The dev compose becomes `brabo-dev`, and dev refuses to come up next to an installation
x: adr 0170 — the dev compose becomes `brabo-dev`, and dev refuses to come up next to an installation adr 0170 — the dev compose becomes brabo-dev, and dev refuses to come up next to an installation status accepted. the maintainer's decision on 2026-09-27 (at-173): "both" — its own name for dev and a guard. it references adr 0150 (the installation compose, which was born saying it had a name different from dev's) and adr 0152 (the volumes that matter). it edits neither. context measured on 2026-09-19: docker/docker-compose.yml (dev) and docker/docker-compose.install.yml both declared name: brabo. the installation compose's comment asserted the opposite — "name diferente do compose de dev de proposito: os dois podem coexistir na mesma maquina" — and it was not true. for docker, a machine with an installation and a checkout had one project: the containers (brabo-api-1, brabo-postgres-1…), the network (brabodefault) and the same-name volumes (brabopgdata, braboneo4jdata, brabogitlocalrepos, braboprojectworkspaces…) were the same. three consequences, the first measured: bringing up one compose over the other recreates the other's containers and connects them to its database — an installation's database received a migration from dev; scripts/dev/reset-total.sh does drop schema … cascade on the postgres of the brabo project — that is, it would delete the installation's database; docker compose down of one brings down the other. the production compose (docker-compose.prod.yml) was already brabo-prod, and is not part of this. decision 1. the dev compose is now called brabo-dev. containers brabo-dev-<servico-1, network brabo-devdefault, volumes brabo-dev<chave. the observability overlay (docker-compose.observability.yml) repeats the name, because the name: of the last -f wins and a different value there would move the whole stack to another project; its alloy filters by com.docker.compose.project=brabo-dev. the installation one stays brabo. it is the name already-made installations have, and changing it would disconnect each of them from their own volumes on the next update — the cost would fall on whoever never read this repository. whoever changes is the developer side, which reads the changelog and has the runbook. 2. a guard, in preflight.mjs and in reset-total.sh. both refuse, naming the containers found and the down (without -v) of each file, when there is on the machine a container — in any state, docker ps -a — whose com.docker.compose.project.configfiles label points to the installation compose (docker-compose.install.yml, or the asset name brabo-install-compose.yml). and they refuse when the dev compose, as the script calls it, would resolve to the brabo project (a composeprojectname=brabo in the .env or in the environment). in the reset, the guard is the first step, even before the preflight, and the refusal comes out as reset nao comecou. the criterion is the label's file, not the project name: an installation is recognized under any -p, and that is what makes the guard useful against what the name does not solve — the dev compose brought up with -p brabo by hand, the composeprojectname, and an old checkout with name: brabo (which does not have this guard, but whose accident the new checkout refuses to continue). the rule exists in two places, js (scripts/dev/instalacao-na-maquina.mjs) and bash (recusarsehainstalacao in scripts/dev/reset-total-lib.sh), because the reset's spec runs with a fake node in the path and needs to prove that the script itself refuses. both are exercised by the specs next to them. docker that does not answer does not refuse: the preflight says the guard did not run and continues (the up brings up nothing without docker), and in the reset the build, still before the first effect, would fail the same way. 3. migration for whoever already develops: a warning, never a refusal, never deleting. the next pnpm dev creates empty brabo-dev volumes; the data stays in the brabo ones. the preflight warns when it fi

only writefile worked, because it writes through the engine process on the host, outside the container. reproduced on real docker (node:22-bookworm-slim, --cap-drop all, folder 755 of uid 1000): as root touch gives permission denied; with --user 1000:1000 it writes. with a uid without an /etc/passwd entry home becomes / and npm dies at //.npm. dockerport has five operations, the bind is one folder of a marked type and the type has no privileged/capadd/free -v (adr 0130). any fix has to fit in that. decision especificacaodecontainer gains usuario?: { uid, gid }. the cli adapter translates it into --user <uid:<gid and --env home=/tmp (constant: a uid without passwd gets home=/). without usuario, run comes out byte for byte as before. the api is who measures, since it reaches the folder (the base mounted by identity, or the managed root): get /internal/projects/:id/container-spec now returns usuariodapasta (stat of the folder; null if it cannot measure, if the project is runner or if the owner is root). the broker composes usuario from that context — never from a request body: start has no body and pedidodeexecvalidado ignores any extra field. the broker revalidates (usuariovalidado): integers in 1..2^31-1, 0 refused naming the field. root is the absent one; an explicit --user 0 would be a loosening nobody decided. exec gets no field: docker exec inherits the container's user. it applies to container and mounted (the api measures the folder each one mounts); runner mode does not go through the broker and does not change. consequences it opens no containment door. the process now has less power over the host than before (non-root instead of root), --cap-drop all stays, and there is no field where a caller writes user, capability, mount or network. the second option considered, giving back dacoverride/chown/fowner, was refused: it loosens the containment adr 0130 fixed and keeps root. a third, the broker doing stat itself, would require mounting the projects' folders in the broker (today it only has the socket) — more surface in a root-equivalent process. the api already reaches them. it is not breaking for the operator: an unreadable or root-owned folder falls into "as always". an already created container does not change until recreated (--user belongs to run); t: ADR 0207 — A gate cycle stalled for more than 2 h parks, and only a human gesture resumes it
x: adr 0207 — a gate cycle stalled for more than 2 h parks, and only a human gesture resumes it adr 0207 — a gate cycle stalled for more than 2 h parks, and only a human gesture resumes it status accepted. 2026-10-02 (at-391, owner decision on 02/10). revises adr 0067 without editing it: automatic rescue continues, with an age ceiling. context adr 0067 made the gaterescuer resume on its own every inprogress cycle stalled for more than 15 min, at boot and on every tick. the real use of 02/10 showed three problems: (1) it restarted a cycle whose session had a proposedaction pending from a qa- actor — the cycle was waiting for a person, the area was paid again and the action would be orphaned; (2) the "live process" test was per project and the row is per task, so a lost cycle went 8 h without rescue because the project's qa lead was alive and idle; (3) there is no ceiling: a cycle nobody looked at for hours is restarted entirely over a context that may have changed. decision alive is per task. the rescue asks the lead ({:emvoo?, taskid}); a lead too busy to answer counts as alive. a pending human decision holds the rescue. a pending action from a gate actor (qa, secops, appsec) in the cycle's session: log only. a 2 h ceiling, by last activity. age counts from updatedat, the same column as the staleness threshold, and not from insertedat: upsert! touches updatedat on every subagent, so a cycle that advances is not old; counting from creation would park long, live cycles. above the ceiling, the row gets parkedat, the session log gets gate.rescueparked (task, gate, age, reason) and the sweep stops seeing it — boot and tick. resuming requires a human gesture, through gaterescuer.retomarestacionado/3. a new in-flight entry of the same cycle clears the mark. consequences there was no human path to resume a gate cycle; the minimum delivered is the engine function, called by the operator. an internal route and a button on the event remain proposed, not done. the pending item is read by session, not by task: proposedactions has no taskid. two tasks in the same session with a pending qa action hold each other — an accepted price, the worst case is not rescuing, never paying twice. rule: rn-722, which revises rn-140.

t: ADR 0208 — Infra inherits the network the Arquiteto declared
x: adr 0208 — infra inherits the network the arquiteto declared adr 0208 — infra inherits the network the arquiteto declared status accepted. 2026-10-02 (at-392; owner decision on 02/10, "direct egress"). revises, without editing them, point 3 of adr 0190 (the server's start-up with a literal network: "none") and departs from §4 of adr 0065, which asked for the user's authorization for egress. context measured on 02/10 (project loja-teste-2): the arquiteto decided artifact.projectimage v1 with network: "egress" ("egress needed for npm install…"). on acceptance of the infra handoff, the server's automatic start-up (subirnoaceite/2, infraleadserver.ex) proposed containerstart with none, and executecontainerstartusecase recorded v2 (infra-lead) with none, overwriting the arquiteto's decision. the node container came up without network, and npm install does not run. decision infra's election inherits the network of the most recent artifact.projectimage emitted by the arquiteto (actorid: "arquiteto"), in any session of the project — read locally by the engine (event.rededoarquiteto/1, the same postgres, no http in the loop). it applies to the server's start-up on acceptance and to the proposecontainerstart tool when the model does not pass network. without an arquiteto decision (or with a value outside none/egress), it stays none, as before. the start-up still happens on its own: adr 0190's containerstart: autoapprove seed does not change, so egress comes up without a click. consequences the price is declared, not paid: the egress network reaches the machine's published ports (adr 0189, edge 5), and the reasoning of external-effect.ts that "without a network, curl sh reaches nothing" stops holding for every project where the arquiteto declared egress. the user consent adr 0065 §4 asked for leaves the path by owner decision. the version recorded by infra now repeats the arquiteto's network instead of downgrading it; the artifact's history stays coherent. rule: rn-723.

t: ADR 0209 — The engine moves up to Elixir 1.20.4 / OTP 29.1.1
x: adr 0209 — the engine moves up to elixir 1.20.4 / otp 29.1.1 adr 0209 — the engine moves up to elixir 1.20.4 / otp 29.1.1 status accepted. 2026-10-02 (at-398; owner decision on 02/10, "move the engine up to otp 29.1.x"). changes the runtime pinned in adr 0024 (decision 10: the same elixir version in the dockerfiles and in ci), without editing it — the single version rule still holds, what changes is the version. context since at-361 the engine's dockerfile.prod runs on alpine 3.24.2 with otp 27.3.4.18 (hexpm does not publish 27.1.2 on 3.24), while dev and ci stayed on elixir 1.17.3 / otp 27.1.2 / alpine 3.20.3. the engine build in ci started aborting in about 10% of runs (0/57 before 821, 5/49 after) with: measured cause: alpine 3.24's musl 1.2.6 refuses the fixed-size alternate signal stack (sigstksz = 8192) that erts 27 requests, on hosts with amx (erlang/otp11349). the fix — sizing by sysconf(scminsigstksz) (commits 3a94587176/fc35c2496c) — exists only from otp 29.1 on. the same defect would make the production engine die at boot on a server with amx: the ci flakiness is the machine lottery. moving alpine back to 3.22 would fix the symptom and freeze the image on a line that stops receiving security fixes; it was not chosen. decision the engine runs elixir 1.20.4 / otp 29.1.1 in dev, production and ci. the image is hexpm/elixir:1.20.4-erlang-29.1.1-alpine-3.24.2, pinned by the index digest (sha256:ad851f40…, adr 0159/0178), the same in the dockerfile.prod builder and in the dev dockerfile. the production runtime stays alpine:3.24.2 (the builder's musl matches the runtime's). elixir 1.20 is the only line with an hexpm image and build for otp 29.1. elixirversion/otpversion go up together in the three workflows that declare them (ci.yml, golden-set-rag.yml, golden-set-qa.yml), and mix.exs now requires ~ 1.20. the "build, scan e smoke" job prints whether the host has amx (grep -c amxtile /proc/cpuinfo): green on a host with amx is the proof that the defect did not come back, and not luck of the draw. no mix.lock dependency changed: mix deps.get + mix compile --warnings-as-errors pass on the new version. elixir 1.20's type checker pointed out a dead clause in engine.agents.filademensagens.acordar/3 — the failure to start the agent raises, it does not come back as a value — and it was fixed by containing the error per agent, not silenced. consequences dev price: the engine's build/deps volumes were compiled with otp 27. mix recompiles on its own what was built with another elixir version, so docker compose up -d --build engine is enough; if the volume insists on old artifacts, docker volume rm of the engine's two volumes. being automatic recompilation, the change is not breaking for operators. whoever runs the engine outside docker needs elixir 1.20.4 / otp 29.1.1 (mix format --check-formatted depends on the version, adr 0024 decision 10). dependabot docker: with otp 29.1 + alpine 3.24 there is no broken pair anymore, and no ignore was added. it may propose a newer otp 29.1.x hexpm/elixir tag — all contain the fix. a proposal that goes down to otp < 29.1 with alpine ≥ 3.24 reintroduces the defect and must be refused in review. a kubernetes rollout mixes, for moments, otp 27 and 29 nodes: erlang distribution accepts pairs up to two major versions apart.

t: ADR 0210 — Text animation with `motion`
x: adr 0210 — text animation with `motion` adr 0210 — text animation with motion status accepted. 2026-10-03 (at-401; owner decision on 03/10: use ai elements' shimmer on every "in progress" text, with the motion lib). context the text saying "the agent is working" ("thinking…", "gathering information…", the "working" status) was static or came with three pulsing dots. the owner chose ai elements' shimmer (<https://elements.ai-sdk.dev/components/shimmer). the original uses motion/react, tailwind and shadcn's cn; brabo's web has no tailwind, shadcn nor clsx — it is css modules over design/tokens.css. decision motion enters apps/web and lives behind one component, apps/web/src/components/ui/shimmer.tsx; no other file imports it. lazymotion + domanimation + m.create(tag) (cached per tag in the module), to load only the dom animation subset. its own vendor group, vendor-motion, in the allow list of codesplitting.groups (at-300). the chunk does not enter the initial load: only the screens that use the shimmer (session, overview, executors) pull it. the gradient uses tokens: base --text-secondary, shine --text-primary. the worst point (the base) is measured in design-contraste.test.ts over --surface-0/1/2, in both themes. this pr applies it to the agent's turn; the loading texts and the other in-progress states come in their own prs. consequences measured weight (pnpm --filter web build): initial index chunk 52.81 → 52.89 kb (16.73 → 16.75 kb gzip); new vendor-motion, 76.23 kb (26.53 kb gzip), outside index.html. reduced motion: usereducedmotion() returns the static text in the base color, and the css module has @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce). the thread's three .typing/.typingdot dots went away; the bpulse keyframe stays, because other components use it.
